facts.statement: The species is known from holotype PVL 6219, which consists of a nearly complete skull articulated with lower jaws and fragmentary postcranial remains.
facts.quote: Lorosuchus is known from the holotype PVL 6219, a nearly complete skull found articulated with the lower jaws and fragmentary postcranial remains.

facts.statement: The fossils were collected at the southern end of the Medina Range, near El Cadillal Lake.

facts.statement: Lorosuchus lived during the Middle to Late Paleocene, approximately 61.7 to 55.8 million years ago.

facts.statement: Phylogenetically, Lorosuchus is recognized as the most basal known member of the sebecid family.
facts.quote: Phylogenetically, Lorosuchus is currently recognized as the basalmost known sebecid.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Diego Pol and Jaime E. Powell in 2011, with the type species being Lorosuchus nodosus.
facts.quote: Lorosuchus was named by Diego Pol and Jaime E. Powell in 2011 and the type species is Lorosuchus nodosus.

facts.statement: The generic name combines 'Loro', referring to the Río Loro Formation, and 'suchus', a Latinized form of the Greek word for the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Loro in reference to the Río Loro Formation in which Lorosuchus was found, and suchus, Latinized from the Greek souchos, an Egyptian crocodile god.
